definition: Tatoeba is a free collection of example sentences with translations geared towards foreign language learners.
details: It is available in more than 400 languages. Its name comes from the Japanese phrase tatoeba (例えば), meaning 'for example'. It is written and maintained by a community of volunteers through a model of open collaboration. Individual contributors are known as "Tatoebans". It is run by Association Tatoeba, a French non-profit organization funded through donations.

explainer.lead: Tatoeba is a free, volunteer-built collection of example sentences with translations for language learners. It matters because it provides openly accessible parallel sentences across hundreds of languages for study and research.

tiers.eli5: It’s like a huge box of example sentences in many languages, each with a translation, made by helpful people for anyone learning a language.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use Tatoeba as a source of parallel sentences for low-resource language pairs or for building example-based lookup tools. A pitfall is that volunteer-contributed translations vary in quality and coverage, so filtering and validation are needed.
tiers.paperLevel: Tatoeba is a community-curated corpus of sentence–translation pairs, available in over 400 languages. Its coverage and quality are uneven because entries are contributed by volunteers under open collaboration.

explainer.example: A learner can look up a Japanese sentence and see its English, French, and Spanish translations, all contributed by volunteers.
